Price of My Pig

Price of the pig?

There’s a jig I know called “The Price of the Pig”, very close to the Scottish tune called “The Hills of Glenorchy”, but it’s very different from this tune.

This is a different tune to the jig ‘The Price of a Pig’

The Price Of My Pig, X:6

Some variations from Michel Balatti & company, mixed into X5.

One time through the A Part they chord the third & fourth bars as:
| [ec][dB][cA] [dB][cA][BG] | [cA][BG][AE] DGF |

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on February 8th, 2020.

The Price Of My Pig, X:7

From the playing of Joshua Dukes.

One time through the A Part he plays the first three bars as “E3 ~A3 | ~B3 ~G3 | cBA BAG |”, and, throws in a few other rolls elsewhere.

↳ Posted by Mike Peckett on March 3rd, 2024.

Re: The Price Of My Pig

I’ve been meaning to resurrect this tune.

I used to follow it with “The Butchers’ March, which gives a nice key change, and end the set with ”Whelan’s Old Sow", which is a good tune to end any set with.

I enjoy the whimsy of putting sets together on the basis of their names. It’s usually possible to arrange them in an order which makes musical sense.

↳ Posted by Roger O'Keeffe on September 4th, 2025.

Re: The Price Of My Pig

It is a lovely tune. Seems to always provides a nice key change, whatever you pair it with. I’ve played it with ‘Out on the Ocean’ quite a few times.

↳ Posted by Matt Milton on September 5th, 2025.

The Price Of My Pig, X:9

I have a recording of The Price Of A Pig played on the Bagpipes, so I decided to add a setting of this tune for the Bagpipes. At Comhaltas Melbourne, we play the 2 tunes as a set and the nickname is “The Piggies”.

↳ Posted by Connor Hickey on January 20th, 2026.
